stakes.name: The Welcome
stakes.blurb: A house tests the stranger before it shows the fault.

stakes.name: The Fault Line
stakes.blurb: Every house carries a crack it has learned to call tradition.

stakes.name: The Reckoning
stakes.blurb: The crack opens, and someone must decide what the house becomes.

storylines.title: The Hoarded Vein
storylines.summary: A heaven-grade vein runs under the pill terraces, and the elders have been quietly drinking from it for a century.

chapters.title: The Seam in the Terraces
chapters.brief: Elder Bai wants the herb terraces walked before the council meets. The earth under the third terrace glows where no lamp was hung.

test.text: Gather three spirit herbs from the terraces

choices.label: Report the seam to Elder Bai.
choices.detail: The old man listens without blinking and writes nothing down. That is how the mountain keeps its books.

choices.label: Show the outer disciples the seam first.
choices.detail: The outer yard has been watering thin soil for years. They deserve to see what the elders have been standing on.

chapters.title: The Council's Silence
chapters.brief: The Traditionalists want the vein sealed and forgotten. The Reformists want it opened to the outer hall. Both blocs have stopped speaking to each other.

test.text: Attune at the shrine to read the vein's qi

choices.label: Stand with the Traditionalists and seal the vault.
choices.detail: A mountain is not a warehouse. What is sealed today can be opened by a wiser hand tomorrow.

choices.label: Stand with the Reformists and open the vault.
choices.detail: The outer disciples will remember who opened the door, and so will the elders who wanted it shut.

chapters.title: The Mountain's Answer
chapters.brief: The council has stalled long enough for the vein to reach the roots of the pill terraces. One furnace-load will decide whether the mountain feeds its children or its vaults.

test.text: Brew one pill from the vein-fed herbs

choices.label: Bind the vein to the sect's own furnaces.
choices.detail: The mountain keeps its promise: every disciple who climbs gets a share of what the mountain gives.

choices.label: Break the seal and let the valley draw.
choices.detail: A vein belongs to the valley that grew over it. The sect will have to earn its pills like everyone else.

endings.title: The Mountain Keeps Its Promise
endings.text: The vein runs into the common furnaces, and for the first time in a century the outer yard smells of its own pills.

endings.title: A Vein Half-Opened
endings.text: The council keeps its vault and grants the outer hall a measured share. Nobody is satisfied, which the elders call balance.

endings.title: The Elders Remember
endings.text: The seam is sealed, the terraces are quiet, and the people who opened their mouths about it are posted to the far gate.

storylines.title: The Honest Edge
storylines.summary: Cliffspire's hardliners keep the gate shut to rootless talent, and a generation of outer disciples has never been given a real blade.

chapters.title: A Duel at the Eastern Pass
chapters.brief: A letter stamped with a sword asks whether your edge is honest. The hardliners will read the answer in how you fight.

test.text: Clear six beasts from the eastern pass

choices.label: Take the hardliners' duel.
choices.detail: One clean cut, no politics. The hardliners respect a blade that speaks before its owner does.

choices.label: Fight beside the outer disciples.
choices.detail: The outer yard has technique and no teacher. Standing in their line tells Cliffspire something the hardliners will not like.

chapters.title: The Blade That Was Promised
chapters.brief: The hardliners commissioned a blade for the gate captain. The outer yard was promised the same steel a decade ago.

test.text: Forge two pieces of work at the anvil

choices.label: Forge for the hardliners' armoury.
choices.detail: A sharp blade in a captain's hand keeps the pass. Whether the pass should be kept is a different question.

choices.label: Teach the outer yard to forge its own.
choices.detail: Steel is not the lesson. The lesson is that they are allowed to hold it.

chapters.title: The Gate and the World
chapters.brief: The sect master is old, the hardliners are loud, and the outer yard has learned to make its own blades. Cliffspire will be one thing or the other by winter.

test.text: Send your answer to the market board

choices.label: Keep Cliffspire closed to outsiders.
choices.detail: The blade is honest because the hand is known. A gate that opens for everyone is a market, not a school.

choices.label: Open the gate to any root.
choices.detail: A hundred years of careful bloodlines has produced one good swordsman and a great many clerks.

endings.title: The Edge Belongs to the Hand
endings.text: Cliffspire opens its yard to rootless talent. The hardliners call it dilution; the outer disciples call it a school.

endings.title: Two Blades in One Hall
endings.text: The gate stays half-shut. The hardliners keep the pass and the outer yard keeps its anvil, and neither disarms the other.

endings.title: The Pass Holds
endings.text: The gate is barred, the promise is forgotten, and the outer yard goes back to practising with wooden swords.

storylines.title: The Poisoned Heir
storylines.summary: Two heirs, one cup, and a house that considers poison a form of etiquette. The wrong answer makes you part of the inheritance.

chapters.title: A Debt at Lotus Lake
chapters.brief: A painted letter asks for fresh herbs, no questions. Half the lake already knows which heir sent it.

test.text: Gather four spirit herbs for the lake house

choices.label: Sell the herbs to the elder heir.
choices.detail: The elder heir pays in old silver and older smiles. The physician of the younger heir pays in nothing at all.

choices.label: Give them to the poisoned heir's physician.
choices.detail: A physician with no silver and a patient with no time. The lake will hear about this by evening.

chapters.title: The Taste of the Tea
chapters.brief: The house's tea is famous. The house's tea is also the reason no rival ever dines twice at Lotus Lake.

test.text: Buy three lots at the market for the house's table

choices.label: Carry the poison to the market.
choices.detail: The lake trades in what it knows. A buyer who does not ask is a buyer who has already been chosen.

choices.label: Test the tea and warn the buyers.
choices.detail: The market will remember a warning longer than it remembers a bargain.

chapters.title: Two Heirs, One Cup
chapters.brief: The younger heir is failing. The elder heir has already ordered the funeral wine, and the cauldron is waiting.

test.text: Brew two doses at the cauldron

choices.label: Brew the antivenom for the poisoned heir.
choices.detail: A cure is a political act. The younger heir will live, and the elder heir will have to explain why that is a surprise.

choices.label: Brew the poison the elders actually ordered.
choices.detail: The lake has one rule for succession and no rule for grief. You are paid either way.

endings.title: The Cup Is Emptied
endings.text: The younger heir lives. Lotus Lake learns that a cure can travel as far as a poison, and the elder heir learns to smile at the wrong time.

endings.title: A House With Two Futures
endings.text: The poison is poured away and the succession is postponed. The lake calls this mercy and keeps the cup polished.

endings.title: The Funeral Wine
endings.text: The younger heir is buried with full ceremony. The elder heir sends you a very expensive thank-you.

storylines.title: The Communion
storylines.summary: Ten Thousand Hoof Plain cannot agree whether the herds are brothers or stock, and the pens are filling either way.

chapters.title: Tracks on the Plain
chapters.brief: The herders have lost three nights of sleep to a herd that will not stay off the road. The communion faction says it is asking for something.

test.text: Drive the plain's beasts away from the road

choices.label: Cull the herd the herders fear.
choices.detail: A dead beast cannot ask for anything. The herders sleep and the pens stay full.

choices.label: Drive them without a kill.
choices.detail: It takes longer and pays less. The herd turns for the hills on its own, and the communion faction notices.

chapters.title: The Pens at Ten Thousand Hoof
chapters.brief: The slave-beast faction has bought new chains. The communion faction has stopped buying anything at all.

test.text: Gather fodder and herbs for the pens

choices.label: Feed the penned beasts first.
choices.detail: A chain is still a chain, but a hungry beast is a dead one. The communion faction calls it a beginning.

choices.label: Sell the fodder to the slave-beast faction.
choices.detail: They pay for what they need and remember who supplied it. The pens get their chains and the plain gets its answer.

chapters.title: Who Speaks for the Herd
chapters.brief: The plain's council will hear one voice from outside the house. The herds have no vote, so someone has to lend them one.

test.text: Listen to the plain at the shrine

choices.label: Stand with the communion faction.
choices.detail: The beasts are people with clearer instincts. A house that forgets this is only a market with better fences.

choices.label: Stand with the breeders.
choices.detail: The house eats because the pens are full. Sentiment does not fill a winter storehouse.

endings.title: The Plain Answers
endings.text: The chains come off the pens. Ten Thousand Hoof becomes the only house whose gate the herds cross by choice.

endings.title: A Shorter Chain
endings.text: The pens stay, the chains are lightened, and the communion faction calls this a first step rather than a victory.

endings.title: The Pens Hold
endings.text: The herds are stock, the council is satisfied, and the plain is quieter than it was.

storylines.title: The Failing Array
storylines.summary: The grand array under Inkstone Plateau is failing, and the house that draws reality has been drawing over the crack for forty years.

chapters.title: The Line That Should Not Bend
chapters.brief: A ward-stone on the southern rim has gone warm. The house's letter calls it routine maintenance and pays too well for routine.

test.text: Cut two replacement ward-stones at the forge

choices.label: Repair the stones quietly.
choices.detail: A crack in a ward is not a crisis if nobody is told. The house pays for silence and calls it professionalism.

choices.label: Take the contract and say nothing.
choices.detail: The letter asked for stones, not questions. The payment is generous enough to buy several answers elsewhere.

chapters.title: A Diagram of Broken Light
chapters.brief: At the shrine the array's light bends the wrong way. Something under the plateau is drawing back.

test.text: Trace the array's circuit at the shrine twice

choices.label: Trace the array to its broken corner.
choices.detail: The flaw has a shape, and the shape has an author. The house will want to know which of its elders drew it.

choices.label: Feed the array your own qi and hide the crack.
choices.detail: A patch is not a repair, but it holds for another season. The house calls that a solution.

chapters.title: The Plateau Answers
chapters.brief: The grand array is one bad night from taking the plateau with it. The house's elders have called a closed session and invited you to the door.

test.text: Walk a hidden realm's altar trial

choices.label: Reveal the failing grand array.
choices.detail: A diagram is a promise. The house can redraw it honestly, or it can keep pretending the line is straight.

choices.label: Keep the secret and take the commission.
choices.detail: The plateau holds for now. The elders pay for the extra season and the silence that comes with it.

endings.title: The Diagram Redrawn
endings.text: Inkstone Plateau admits the flaw and redraws the array in public. The elders lose face; the plateau keeps its mountain.

endings.title: A Patch of Light
endings.text: The crack is patched and the elders keep their seats. The array holds, and everyone agrees not to ask for how long.

endings.title: The Line Holds
endings.text: The secret is kept, the commission is paid, and the plateau is left to the arithmetic of another season.

storylines.title: Succession by Murder
storylines.summary: Blood Moon's master is dead by doctrine and the new heir needs a witness with clean hands and a full purse.

chapters.title: The Blood-Swamp Court
chapters.brief: The letter is written on red paper and smells of iron. The new heir wants the marsh road cleared before the funeral.

test.text: Clear nine beasts from the blood-swamp road

choices.label: Kneel to the new heir.
choices.detail: The court has already decided. A knee costs nothing and the purse is heavy.

choices.label: Refuse the knee and walk out.
choices.detail: The marsh hears everything. A house that cannot buy your knee may decide to take something else.

chapters.title: A Cup for the Old Master
chapters.brief: The funeral cup is being prepared. The heir wants it to taste of remembrance, and the old master's rivals want it to taste of nothing at all.

test.text: Brew two funeral doses at the cauldron

choices.label: Brew what the heir asks.
choices.detail: The cup will be remembered. So will the hand that filled it.

choices.label: Brew something harmless.
choices.detail: The old master is dead already. The cup does not need to kill anyone else.

chapters.title: The Crimson Moon Rite
chapters.brief: The rite needs a body that has walked a hidden realm and come back with something the swamp can drink.

test.text: Stand an altar trial and bring back its legacy

choices.label: Take the blood rite.
choices.detail: Power is taken, never given. The rite will mark you as surely as it marks the heir.

choices.label: Break the cup and end the succession.
choices.detail: A doctrine built on murder has one flaw: it always needs another murderer. Break the cup and let the swamp choose something else.

endings.title: The Moon Drinks
endings.text: The rite is taken and the heir rules with your mark on the court. Blood Moon remembers its friends, and its friends do not sleep well.

endings.title: A Court With a Witness
endings.text: The succession stands and the cup is broken. The swamp calls it an accident and the heir calls it a debt.

endings.title: The Cup Breaks
endings.text: The rite is refused and the court closes its doors. Blood Moon has a long memory and a longer list of people who owe it.

storylines.title: The Plague They Made
storylines.summary: Green Hollow has a cure for the plague in the eastern villages. Green Hollow also has the plague's original recipe.

chapters.title: A Village Without a Name
chapters.brief: A valley letter asks for herbs in quantities that suggest a clinic, not a garden. The villages east of the market have started burning their dead.

test.text: Gather six spirit herbs for the valley

choices.label: Gather for the valley's own stores.
choices.detail: The valley pays promptly and asks for a receipt. The villages are not mentioned in the letter.

choices.label: Gather for the sick villages.
choices.detail: The valley will call it waste. The villages will call it something else.

chapters.title: The Price of a Cure
chapters.brief: The cure works. The valley has priced it by the patient's village, and the eastern villages have started paying in land.

test.text: Brew three doses of the valley's cure

choices.label: Sell the cure at the valley's price.
choices.detail: A monopoly is only a problem for the people outside it. The ledger balances.

choices.label: Give the cure away.
choices.detail: The valley will send someone to explain economics. The villages will send people who are still alive.

chapters.title: The Plague's Author
chapters.brief: The plague's strain matches a valley recipe book, and the page has an elder's seal. The valley wants the book back.

test.text: Send your finding to the market board

choices.label: Name the valley's elder.
choices.detail: A cure is a gift. A plague is a business plan. The market deserves to know which one it has been buying.

choices.label: Bury the proof and take the valley's thanks.
choices.detail: The plague is over. The valley will pay generously for a history that ends with the cure.

endings.title: The Cure Is Public
endings.text: The recipe is read aloud in every market east of the pass. Green Hollow loses its monopoly and keeps its name.

endings.title: The Valley Pays
endings.text: The cure reaches the villages at a price they can survive. The valley calls it charity and keeps the recipe locked.

endings.title: The Book Closes
endings.text: The proof disappears, the valley thanks you, and the eastern villages remember a plague that nobody caused.

storylines.title: The Seller of Secrets
storylines.summary: Someone under the market is selling all twelve houses' business to each other, and Shadow Veil would like to know who before the houses do.

chapters.title: A Name in the Undermarket
chapters.brief: A note under the stall door offers a secret about the stall next door. The price is three ordinary purchases and one unusual question.

test.text: Make three purchases to cover a trail

choices.label: Buy the first secret.
choices.detail: Information is the only real currency. The seller takes the silver and leaves a name that is probably true.

choices.label: Follow the seller instead.
choices.detail: A bought secret is a leash. Following the seller is a chance to cut it.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Faces
chapters.brief: The seller's ledger names a market clerk, two gate guards, and someone who signs letters for the Azure Cloud.

test.text: Read the notice board for the seller's next drop

choices.label: Trade the market's ledger to the Veil.
choices.detail: The Veil pays for what it cannot steal. The market will not notice until its prices move without it.

choices.label: Warn the market watch.
choices.detail: The watch is not subtle, but a clerk who sells gate schedules is worse.

chapters.title: The Veil Lifts
chapters.brief: The seller is ready to leave the province with twelve houses' secrets. Shadow Veil wants the seller stopped, and the ledger.

test.text: Clear the seller's escort from the under-city road

choices.label: Take the Veil's offer and vanish.
choices.detail: The Veil offers a new face and a share of the ledger. The province will forget you before the season turns.

choices.label: Expose the seller to all twelve houses.
choices.detail: Every house will want the ledger. Every house will owe the person who put it on the board.

endings.title: The Ledger Changes Hands
endings.text: The seller is gone and the ledger is with the Veil. The under-market has a new silence, and you know what it costs.

endings.title: Twelve Houses Owe a Name
endings.text: The ledger is read on the board. Half the province is embarrassed and the other half is taking notes.

endings.title: The Seller Walks
endings.text: The seller leaves with the secrets and the Veil remembers that you were paid not to follow.

storylines.title: The Rented Sky
storylines.summary: Stormcrown can call a tribulation down on anyone with the silver, and the villages under the cloud have started paying not to be chosen.

chapters.title: A Storm With a Price
chapters.brief: The peak's letter quotes a fee for a guided tribulation and a discount for silence. The shrine has been crackling for three nights.

test.text: Read the storm's charge at the shrine twice

choices.label: Pay for a guided tribulation.
choices.detail: The sky is a service. The peak delivers on time, and the receipt is written in scorch marks.

choices.label: Refuse and study the storm yourself.
choices.detail: Lightning is courted, not commanded. The peak respects a client who reads the terms.

chapters.title: The Hour They Rent
chapters.brief: A village has paid the peak to aim a tribulation at a rival village. The invoice is signed and the cloud is already forming.

test.text: Clear the storm road of beasts before the cloud gathers

choices.label: Bring the peak a worthy subject.
choices.detail: A tribulation needs a body. A beast is cheaper than a village and the peak does not ask questions.

choices.label: Warn the villages under the cloud.
choices.detail: The peak will call it breach of contract. The villages will call it something they can survive.

chapters.title: Judgment, Personally
chapters.brief: The Sovereign will hear one petition before the storm season. Every village on the plain has sent someone, and the peak has sent a price list.

test.text: Stand an altar trial under the storm

choices.label: Take the Sovereign's thunder.
choices.detail: Judgment must be delivered personally. The peak will teach you how to hold it.

choices.label: Break the monopoly of the sky.
choices.detail: A tribulation is a test, not a service. The peak has been selling the heavens' own weather.

endings.title: The Sky Is Not for Rent
endings.text: The storm season opens to everyone. Stormcrown keeps its peaks and loses its price list.

endings.title: A Fair Price for Thunder
endings.text: The peak still sells tribulations, but the villages set the terms. The Sovereign calls it a compromise and the plain calls it a start.

endings.title: The Invoice Stands
endings.text: The cloud gathers over the village that could not pay. The peak sends you a receipt and a discount for next season.

storylines.title: The Thawing Elder
storylines.summary: An elder is coming out of a century of ice, and Frozen Heaven would rather she stayed a perfectly preserved lesson.

chapters.title: A Vault That Breathes
chapters.brief: The glacier vaults have kept a hundred years of stores at perfect stillness. One vault has started to breathe.

test.text: Gather four herbs that will survive the cold

choices.label: Preserve the vault's stores.
choices.detail: Emotion is impurity. A vault that stays cold keeps everything worth keeping.

choices.label: Take the thawing elder what she asks for.
choices.detail: She asked for warm tea and a name. The vault keepers have not decided which request is more dangerous.

chapters.title: The Sound of a Heart
chapters.brief: The elder remembers a student, a season, and a name the sect has spent a century erasing. The ice is thinner every morning.

test.text: Sit with the shrine's stillness

choices.label: Help the elder remember.
choices.detail: A memory is not a contagion, whatever the scripture says. The vault keepers are already sharpening their needles.

choices.label: Refreeze her and report it.
choices.detail: The sect's doctrine is clear: feeling is the impurity that slows the freeze. The report will be filed and the vault will be quiet.

chapters.title: What Emotion Costs
chapters.brief: The elder will either wake or be ice by dawn. Frozen Heaven has sent no instruction, which is its own instruction.

test.text: Brew two warming draughts at the cauldron

choices.label: Let her thaw.
choices.detail: A sect that preserves everything will eventually preserve nothing alive. The glacier can spare one warm body.

choices.label: Let the ice keep its silence.
choices.detail: The vault is cold, the doctrine holds, and the sect pays for the frost it understands.

endings.title: The Glacier Thaws
endings.text: The elder wakes, and Frozen Heaven discovers that a heart can survive a century if someone remembers to warm it.

endings.title: One Vault Left Open
endings.text: The elder wakes for a season and chooses the ice again. The sect calls it discipline; she calls it a visit.

endings.title: Perfect Stillness
endings.text: The vault is sealed and the elder is a lesson again. The glacier is very quiet, and very proud of it.

storylines.title: The God-Killing Commission
storylines.summary: Furnace City has accepted a commission for a weapon that can kill gods, and the client has paid in advance.

chapters.title: A Commission With No Name
chapters.brief: The order is for a blade with no wielder named and no purpose written. The gold is real and the client is not.

test.text: Complete three pieces of forge work

choices.label: Take the commission.
choices.detail: Creation outranks cultivation. A smith does not ask what the blade will cut.

choices.label: Ask who the weapon is for.
choices.detail: A question is not a refusal. The Cauldron respects a smith who reads the order twice.

chapters.title: The Metal That Remembers
chapters.brief: The ore came from a ruin older than the houses. It rings when no one strikes it, and the forge master has stopped sleeping.

test.text: Keep the forge road clear of beasts

choices.label: Guard the forge road for the Cauldron.
choices.detail: The work must continue. Whatever the metal remembers, it will remember after the blade is finished.

choices.label: Escort the ore caravan instead.
choices.detail: The road is safer with the ore on it than the ore in the forge. The client will have to wait.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Refinements
chapters.brief: The blade is one fold from finished. The forge master has left the final strike to you, and the client has arrived without a face.

test.text: Walk an altar trial for the blade's final temper

choices.label: Finish the weapon.
choices.detail: A commission is a promise. What the client does with it is the client's business, and the Cauldron's name will be on the steel.

choices.label: Sabotage the blade.
choices.detail: A weapon that can kill gods should not be sold to someone who will not give a name.

endings.title: The Steel Remembers
endings.text: The blade is finished and the client takes it without a word. Furnace City is paid, and the forge master starts sleeping again.

endings.title: A Flaw in the Fold
endings.text: The blade leaves the city with a flaw only a master would find. The Cauldron keeps its commission and its deniability.

endings.title: The Commission Closes
endings.text: The weapon is broken in the quench and the client is told to commission elsewhere. Furnace City keeps the gold and loses the name.

storylines.title: The Book That Rewrites
storylines.summary: The Floating Archive holds a book that edits its readers, and the Pavilion wants a copy made by someone who has not read it.

chapters.title: A Library That Drifts
chapters.brief: The archive's letter is a copying commission with a page count and no title. The Pavilion pays by the character and asks for a steady hand.

test.text: Answer the archive at the market board

choices.label: Request a copying commission.
choices.detail: Knowledge must be catalogued, not owned. The Pavilion has a page for everyone, and a price for every page.

choices.label: Ask what the archive is hiding.
choices.detail: A library that drifts between peaks is not hiding a book. It is hiding a reader.

chapters.title: The Page That Reads Back
chapters.brief: The page has no author and no ink. It is warm to the touch, and the copy you have not made yet is already on it.

test.text: Steady your mind at the shrine twice

choices.label: Read the page aloud.
choices.detail: A sentence read aloud can edit a target out of the scene. The question is who is holding the pen.

choices.label: Copy it without reading.
choices.detail: The Pavilion asked for a copy, not a reader. The hand can be steady and the eyes can be closed.

chapters.title: The Reader Rewritten
chapters.brief: The book has begun to write back. The Pavilion's archivist has not been seen for nine days, and the archive has drifted closer to the market.

test.text: Walk an altar trial and keep your name

choices.label: Let the book finish you.
choices.detail: Whoever finishes the book decides what cultivation is. The Pavilion has been waiting a long time for a reader who volunteered.

choices.label: Burn the page.
choices.detail: Some knowledge should be catalogued and never opened. The archive will survive the loss; its readers may not.

endings.title: A Reader Finishes
endings.text: The book closes with your name in it. The archive drifts away, and the Pavilion begins to catalogue a reader instead of a page.

endings.title: The Page Is Copied
endings.text: The copy is shelved and the original is sealed. The archive keeps its secret and you keep your name, for now.

endings.title: The Page Burns
endings.text: The book is ash and the archivist is still missing. The Pavilion thanks you for the fire and does not open the door again.
